blocks.text: intro
sparse, slow, single banjo pluck, tuba sustains, breath between phrases, faint room tone
verse 1
Drunkard alone, weathered, confessional, half-spoken, intimate cabaret register

My folks grew up as the sirens screamed
Sheltered from that haunting dream
Hands clasped tight, hide just in case
Brace
hammered metal struck on "Brace," allowed to ring out into the silence

But the bracing was the wound
The bunker was the bleed
A muscle held taut for years
A cramp you can't release
chorus
quiet foot stomp on the four, accordion swells, instrumentation lifts around the solo voice

So be careful what you wish for
Something is finally listening
Welcome to the next cataclysm
Welcome to the new survivalism
verse 2
instrumentation pulls back, banjo alone, voice more isolated

COVID came and we sheltered too
Dutiful kids, knew what to do
Drained our savings, dabbled in conspiracy
But you totally didn't hear that from me

We shared a frame
That was mostly the same
And even grading on a curve
We cracked our final nerve
chorus
same lift, accordion and suitcase kick around the solo voice

So be careful what you wish for
Something is finally listening
Welcome to the next cataclysm
Welcome to the new survivalism
verse 3
texture corrodes: mechanical clatter enters, slight distortion creeping in around the voice

I was paid to bring the eyeballs in
Truth and lies didn't matter to them
I engineered the surge, watched the discourse spark
Watched my bosses cash in on the lark

I made the click, I took the pay
Sat with the emptiness before that went away
Now you don't need a writer like me
The machine is the only thing they came to see
bridge
percussive, washboard prominent, suitcase kick, voice goes chant-like and rhythmic

They were cramped from holding on too tight
Bracing for the wrong fight every night
We stayed slack soft and small
The muscle that mattered, never trained at all
outro
instrumentation strips back, voice over single sustained tuba tone, radio crackle building underneath

There's a fork in the road ahead
There won't be a sign to read
No voice from outside will tell you
Look within for what you need
voice gets more intimate, almost confidential

Look within
Look within
Look within
final line whispered, almost spoken, no instrumentation
Stay tuned in
fades on radio tone and static

notebook.style: Cabaret, slow and spacious with a brooding, hollow pulse; folk textures open the track, then corrode into slight distortion, mechanical clatter, radio crackle, static, and modern dread, Deep tuba sustains, plucked banjo, breathy accordion chords, washboard scrapes, decaying hammered metal, suitcase kick, and occasional foot-stomp accents frame a single weathered voice in an Urban European cabaret register, half-spoken, breathy, paused, and intimately confessional; close vocal presence, hushed small-room ambience, deep low end, and a fading radio tone
